Why go: a slow day on the water with lunch from the catch

This is the relaxed way to fish on Koh Samui. A traditional wooden Thai fishing boat leaves Big Buddha pier mid-morning and anchors at two spots off the north coast, with an English-speaking guide and crew who bait hooks, untangle lines and help land fish. Lunch is cooked on board, and anything big enough goes onto the plate. Most guests catch something; the fun is the day out on a working boat as much as the fish.

Everything is supplied, and no experience is needed. Groups who want the boat to themselves can book it privately, and there are night squid trips and Saturday deep-sea outings on request.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: families, first-time anglers and groups of friends who want an easy, social day.
  • Choose something else if you want serious sport fishing: trolling is only done on private trips. Our fishing guide covers the options.
  • Prone to seasickness? An anchored boat rolls more than a moving one; take tablets before you board.

Good to know

  • Sun: shade on deck is limited; a hat and a long-sleeve shirt matter more than sunscreen alone.
  • Hooks: keep children back while lines are being cast and reeled in.
  • Weather: February to September is usually calmest. From October to December the north coast catches the monsoon wind.
  • Catch: small fish are released. Ask the crew before you keep anything for a restaurant to cook.

Making the most of the day

Fish bite best on a moving tide, so the crew may change spots several times. Listen to how they want you to hold the line; Thai handline and light-rod techniques feel different from fishing at home. If you keep a larger fish, ask the guide which local restaurant will cook it for you that evening.
